tasks.short: Match Rabobank statement lines to AFAS invoices and payments, clear what does not match.

steps.what: Download CAMT.053 statements from Rabobank and import them into AFAS
Run AFAS auto-match on reference, IBAN, invoice number and amounts
Match remaining lines by hand, searching invoices, agency payments and mail

loop.input: one unmatched bank line plus candidate open items, remittance text and recent mails from the counterparty
loop.output: proposed match or split with a one-line reason, or 'no match'
loop.check: amounts must sum exactly (or within the set tolerance) to the bank line; counterparty IBAN must belong to the proposed relation; otherwise rejected
loop.stop: one pass per line, max 3 candidates; low confidence or failed check goes to the person as unmatched
loop.why_not_simpler: the residue after AFAS rules has free-text descriptions, partial and combined payments and typos that fixed rules do not cover

steps.what: Keep an Excel list of open bank items and ask colleagues what they are
Check the bank balance agrees with the ledger and sign off

tasks.design: Connect Rabobank to AFAS with a daily automatic statement import and tune AFAS match rules and tolerances. A scheduled job on the governed data platform takes the unmatched lines, runs a bounded model step that proposes a match with a reason, and drops it in a review queue; open items older than a set number of days trigger a Teams notification to the owner. The Excel open-items list becomes a Power BI page with balance agreement per account.
tasks.previous_blocker: AFAS rules clear the clean lines, but the residue is free text, combined payments and agency payments that rules miss, so people kept an Excel list.
tasks.enabler_now: Cheap model calls can read payment descriptions and remittance text and propose matches that code then checks to the cent.
tasks.still_hard: Payments with no reference at all and unclear counterparties still need a person to ask around; tuning tolerances without hiding real errors.
tasks.human_edge: Knows which customer pays several invoices in one go, and when a payment that looks wrong is actually a known deal.

ambition.what: Reconcile the bank daily instead of weekly, so collections sees who paid the same day.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper reviews a short queue of proposals each morning instead of hunting lines, and gets the right to set match tolerances within limits the controller signs.

reach.learn: Which unmatched receipts are really customer payments, so dunning stops for customers who already paid.

evidence.claim: AFAS matches CAMT.053 lines on payment reference, IBAN, invoice number, then oldest-first sums; misses go to a person
AP should run with people on exceptions and log every decision with its data
Models can propose matches for free-text bank lines

assumptions: Noordhaven uses AFAS bank matching but imports statements by hand today
Most bank lines are cleared by existing AFAS rules
unknowns: Current share of bank lines matched automatically in AFAS
Number of bank accounts and administrations
Whether a data platform already exists or must be set up
research_questions: What share of bank lines stays unmatched after AFAS rules, per month?
How many of those could a person match from information already in AFAS or mail?
Does Rabobank offer a direct statement feed to AFAS for all Noordhaven accounts?

tasks.short: Run the trial balance in AFAS, compare with subledgers and last month, explain and fix differences.

steps.what: Run trial balance per administration in AFAS
Export to Excel, tie out to AP, AR, bank and prior month
Investigate differences, suspense accounts and odd movements

loop.input: accounts with a difference or a movement above threshold, with their journal lines
loop.output: short draft explanation per account naming the entries that drive it
loop.check: every cited entry must exist and the cited amounts must add up to the movement; else marked unexplained
loop.stop: one draft per flagged account, no retries; unexplained items go to the person
loop.why_not_simpler: code finds the differences, but grouping journal lines into a readable reason needs reading descriptions

steps.what: Post correcting entries after accountant approval
Send trial balance pack to accountant and controller

tasks.design: A nightly job on the governed data platform pulls the AFAS trial balance and subledger balances through the AFAS API and shows tie-outs and month-on-month movements in a Power BI close page, replacing the Excel tie-out. Flagged accounts get a bounded model-drafted explanation that the bookkeeper edits; corrections stay manual in AFAS with accountant approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: AFAS produces the report, but the tie-out to subledgers and the explanations lived in Excel each month, built by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes a small tie-out job and dashboard cheap to build; models can draft variance notes from journal lines.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding whether a difference is a timing issue or an error, and judging accruals; the auditor must accept the new tie-out.
tasks.human_edge: Knows the history behind odd accounts and which differences the auditor will ask about.

ambition.what: A weekly soft trial balance during the month, so the close starts with fewer surprises.

tasks.altitude: Week of close moves from building Excel to reviewing flagged accounts; the bookkeeper proposes corrections directly to the accountant with evidence attached.

reach.learn: Which accruals and cut-off rules cause the recurring trial balance differences.

evidence.claim: Trial balance and subledger tie-outs are standard deterministic reporting
Power BI already runs on a nightly AFAS extract at Noordhaven

assumptions: Power BI AFAS extract can be extended with ledger and subledger balances
Several administrations exist per site or entity
unknowns: How many administrations and ledger accounts are closed monthly
What the external auditor requires as tie-out evidence
research_questions: How many hours per close go to the Excel tie-out today?
Which accounts produce differences most months, and why?
Will the auditor accept a Power BI tie-out as close evidence?

tasks.short: Keep records of own stock (packaging, pallets, diesel, parts) and value it in AFAS.

steps.what: Collect stock counts and movement lists from the three sites
Price and value stock in Excel with AFAS purchase prices
Chase count differences with site managers
Post stock movement and valuation journal in AFAS

tasks.design: Site staff enter counts in a small form app (Power Apps on Microsoft 365) instead of mailing Excel; a scheduled job values counts with the latest AFAS purchase prices, flags differences above a threshold to the site lead in Teams, and prepares the stock journal for the bookkeeper to approve and post in AFAS.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counts arrive as mailed sheets in different formats per site, so pricing and posting were done by hand in Excel.
tasks.enabler_now: A simple form app and valuation job are now cheap to build with AI coding on tools Noordhaven already licenses.
tasks.still_hard: Getting site staff to count on time and consistently; real shrinkage or theft needs a conversation, not a rule.
tasks.human_edge: Judges whether a count gap is a counting error, a missed booking or real loss, and talks to the site manager about it.

ambition.what: Monthly instead of quarterly valuation of pallets and packaging per site.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper stops retyping counts and spends the time on the few differences that matter; nothing else changes in decision rights.

reach.learn: Packaging and pallet usage per site as an input to cost forecasts.

evidence.claim: Stock count capture and valuation are deterministic once counts are structured

assumptions: Customer goods in the warehouses are tracked in a warehouse system, not by finance
Finance only values Noordhaven's own stock such as packaging, pallets, diesel and spare parts
unknowns: Whether a warehouse management system exists and holds own stock
Which stock items are on the balance sheet and how often they are counted
research_questions: Which stock does finance actually record, and what is its value?
Can counts come straight from a warehouse or fuel system instead of a form?
How large are count differences today, and how often are they explained?

tasks.short: Enter, code, match and route purchase and agency invoices in AFAS for approval and payment.

steps.what: Pick invoices from AP mailbox and upload to AFAS Scan & herken
Check recognised fields, code ledger account, cost centre and VAT

loop.input: PDF invoice text, supplier history of coding in AFAS
loop.output: proposed ledger account, cost centre and VAT code with reason
loop.check: code must exist in the administration and VAT code must fit supplier country and reverse-charge rules; repeat suppliers compared to history
loop.stop: one proposal per invoice; low confidence or a check failure goes to the person uncoded
loop.why_not_simpler: UBL invoices with an order match need no model, but PDF invoices without order lines need reading to code

steps.what: Match to order or receipt and route to budget holder for approval
Check agency invoices against hours and split the g-rekening share
Chase approvers and answer supplier payment questions

loop.input: supplier mail plus invoice and payment status from AFAS
loop.output: draft reply with status and expected payment date
loop.check: invoice number and amount must match AFAS; no reply sent without bookkeeper click
loop.stop: one draft per mail; unclear requests left undrafted
loop.why_not_simpler: supplier mails are free text in Dutch and English and must be tied to the right invoice

tasks.design: Configure AFAS to take UBL and Peppol invoices straight in, auto-post one-to-one order matches and run the approval workflow with reminders instead of mail. A scheduled job on the governed data platform compares agency invoices with the agency portal hours, computes the g-rekening split and passes only differences to the bookkeeper; a bounded model step proposes coding for PDF invoices and drafts replies to supplier status questions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Many invoices arrive as PDF without order lines, approvals ran by mail, and agency invoices could only be checked against hours by hand in Excel.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS Scan & herken and order matching are in the product; cheap model calls code PDFs; AI coding makes the agency hours check quick to build.
tasks.still_hard: Budget holders who do not approve on time; suppliers who keep sending PDFs; per-administration VAT and ledger exceptions that keep touchless rates down.
tasks.human_edge: Spots an invoice that looks right but is not, such as a changed IBAN or a double bill from an agency, and knows the supplier to call.

ambition.what: A weekly flex-labour cost check for site managers: agency hours billed versus hours worked, per agency.

tasks.altitude: From keying invoices to owning match rules, tolerances and supplier data; the bookkeeper may approve supplier master data changes after a callback check.

reach.learn: How agency hours relate to site time records, so mismatches are caught before invoices arrive.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 reads UBL and PDF invoices to line level and posts and approves one-to-one matches
AFAS Scan & herken turns a PDF into an e-invoice, finds the supplier by KvK, VAT and IBAN; gaps filled by hand
Escalante Golf went from 2.5 minutes to 45 seconds per invoice with suggested coding reviewed by the team
70% of Dutch respondents approve invoices on paper or by email; 43% say this delays payment
Booking proposals often deliver disappointing touchless shares due to own accounts, VAT codes and exceptions
Inlenersaansprakelijkheid limited by paying the wage tax and VAT part into the agency's g-rekening

assumptions: Invoice volume is several thousand a year across three sites
Agency portals allow an export of approved hours
unknowns: Share of invoices arriving as UBL versus PDF
Whether AFAS Profit 8 order matching is licensed and configured
Whether purchase orders are used for most spend
research_questions: What share of invoices has a purchase order to match against?
How often do agency invoices differ from portal hours, and by how much?
Which AFAS modules and licences does Noordhaven have for Scan & herken and approval workflows?
What is the measured touchless rate after three months of AFAS matching?

role.altitude: The bookkeeper moves from keying invoices and matching bank lines to running exception queues, keeping supplier data clean and setting match rules and tolerances within limits the controller signs.
reach: Collections: share daily cleared receipts so dunning stops for customers who paid
Payroll: tie flex-worker hours to agency invoices
Accountant: supply trial balance tie-outs and variance notes for the close
skills_to_grow: Configuring AFAS match rules, tolerances and approval workflows
Reading and acting on Power BI exception dashboards
Supplier master data control, including IBAN-name check results
Reviewing model proposals critically and logging the decision
role.ambitious_version: A three-person team that processes most invoices without touch, reconciles the bank daily, runs a weekly flex-labour cost check for the sites, and cuts days to close by owning a weekly soft trial balance.
